head: 0b5b2cd0050d3dd3731bc163d422c236a27c2887
claim: On Wayland, where /dev/uinput is unavailable and the session portal offers a RemoteDesktop keyboard, typing reaches the portal with no uinput device open; where uinput works nothing changes

steps.start: a Wayland session whose portal offers a RemoteDesktop keyboard, on a private bus
steps: the engine opens a keyboard-only RemoteDesktop portal session
the client's keys 35, 35, 30, 30 are sent through the engine
the mock portal receives them in order and the session closes on drop
capabilities report uinput when it works and the portal keyboard only when it does not
steps.result: keys reach the portal with no uinput device open; pointer and wheel stay on uinput where it exists

verdicts.seen: Row 2 reads "uinput missing: mechanism=portal-remotedesktop ... keyboard=True ... grant=portal", which matches the Wayland case where the portal provides the keyboard. Row 1 reads "uinput works: mechanism=inputtino/uinput ... keyboard=True ... grant=granted", which matches the unchanged uinput case. The parenthetical under row 2 ("no portal at all, real binary, private bus") conflicts with the portal mechanism on that same row, and the screenshot does not show an open device, so some doubt remains.

The output reads "asserted: no /dev/uinput file descriptor open while the portal carried the keys" and "keys 35,35,30,30 reached the portal in order". That matches the Wayland portal-keyboard part of the outcome. It shows nothing about the uinput-works case, so it covers only the first part.

Read 3 capability entries and 2 test result blocks. Entry 3 shows grant "portal", mechanism "portal-remotedesktop", keyboard true, and the test keys_reach_the_portal_in_order_and_the_session_closes reports ok, which covers the Wayland portal keyboard part. Entry 2 shows grant "granted", mechanism "inputtino/uinput", keyboard true, pointer true, and no unavailable_reason, which covers the uinput-works part. Entry 1 (grant "missing-device-access", reason "no /dev/uinput") matches the outcome's unavailable-uinput condition and is not a contradiction. No failures appear in the output.
